predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the duchy as it stood in 1260: Brabant between Leuven, Brussels, Antwerp and 's-Hertogenbosch

successors.name: Duchy of Burgundy
successors.text: 'In 1430 the Duchies of Lower Lotharingia, Brabant and Limburg were inherited by' Philip the Good (Duchy of Brabant page)

ledger.x: 1260: Cliopatria's Brabant begins, the duchy between Leuven, Brussels, Antwerp and 's-Hertogenbosch.
1283: the Limburg contest opens when Brabant buys the claim.
1289: the Limburg contest ends with the annexation ('The Duchy of Limburg was added to the Duchy of Brabant in 1289'); Guelders renounced its claims.
1402: a southern strip joins Brabant in Cliopatria's outline.
1406: Anthony of Burgundy becomes Duke of Brabant.
1415: the southern strip leaves Brabant in Cliopatria's outline.
1430: Brabant passes to Philip the Good of Burgundy.

wars.name: War of the Limburg Succession (Battle of Worringen)
wars.outcome: Brabant won on 5 June 1288: 'Archbishop Siegfried was taken prisoner by John of Brabant and delivered to Adolf of Berg', 'Reginald of Guelders was released after he had renounced all claims to the Duchy of Limburg', and 'The Duchy of Limburg was added to the…

wars.name: Flemish invasion of Brabant
wars.outcome: A 'military incursion in 1356 into Brabant by Louis II of Flanders' ended with 'the humiliating Treaty of Ath, which ceded Mechelen and Antwerp to Louis'; the page gives no year for the treaty and Cliopatria's outline does not show the loss.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened.
